claim: Endothelial cells (ECs) can still invade if actin polymerization is inhibited.
source: Surprisingly, endothelial cells (ECs) can still invade if actin polymerization is inhibited.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a surprising observation that motivates the study.

claim: Endothelial tip cells employ an alternative mechanism of cell migration that is dependent on Aquaporin (Aqp)-mediated water inflow and increase in hydrostatic pressure.
source: In this study, we show that endothelial tip cells employ an alternative mechanism of cell migration that is dependent on Aquaporin (Aqp)-mediated water inflow and increase in hydrostatic pressure.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: In the zebrafish, ECs express aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 in newly formed vascular sprouts in a VEGFR2-dependent manner.
source: In the zebrafish, ECs express aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 in newly formed vascular sprouts in a VEGFR2-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 loss-of-function studies show an impairment in intersegmental vessels formation because of a decreased capacity of tip cells to increase their cytoplasmic volume and generate membrane protrusions.
source: Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 loss-of-function studies show an impairment in intersegmental vessels formation because of a decreased capacity of tip cells to increase their cytoplasmic volume and generate membrane protrusions, leading to delayed tip cell emergence from the dorsal aorta and slower migration.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 3, 4, and 5.

claim: Loss of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 leads to delayed tip cell emergence from the dorsal aorta and slower migration.
source: Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 loss-of-function studies show an impairment in intersegmental vessels formation because of a decreased capacity of tip cells to increase their cytoplasmic volume and generate membrane protrusions, leading to delayed tip cell emergence from the dorsal aorta and slower migration.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: Further inhibition of actin polymerization resulted in a greater decrease in sprouting angiogenesis, indicating that ECs employ two mechanisms for robust cell migration in vivo.
source: Further inhibition of actin polymerization resulted in a greater decrease in sprouting angiogenesis, indicating that ECs employ two mechanisms for robust cell migration in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Hydrostatic pressure plays an important role in tissue morphogenesis.
source: Our study thus highlights an important role of hydrostatic pressure in tissue morphogenesis.
evidence: This is the concluding statement of the abstract summarizing the broader implication of the findings.

claim: During sprouting angiogenesis, endothelial tip cells generate numerous membrane protrusions such as filopodia and lamellipodia that drive migration and anastomosis.
source: At the initial phase of sprouting angiogenesis, endothelial tip cells generate numerous membrane protrusions such as filopodia and lamellipodia that drive migration and anastomosis (Figueiredo et al., 2021; Gerhardt et al., 2003; Phng et al., 2013; Sauteur et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: During tubulogenesis, apical membranes deform by generating inverse blebs to expand lumens so that blood can be transported efficiently through the blood vascular network.
source: During tubulogenesis, apical membranes deform by generating inverse blebs to expand lumens so that blood can be transported efficiently through the blood vascular network (Gebala et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Following vessel perfusion, ECs become less dynamic and instead develop mechanoresistance to the deforming forces of blood pressure to maintain vessel morphology.
source: However, following vessel perfusion, ECs become less dynamic and instead develop mechanoresistance to the deforming forces of blood pressure to maintain vessel morphology (Kondrychyn et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Localized remodeling of actin cytoskeleton and non-myosin II contractility are instrumental in driving cell shape changes during tissue morphogenesis.
source: It is well established that localized remodeling of actin cytoskeleton and non-myosin II contractility are instrumental in driving cell shape changes during tissue morphogenesis (Clarke and Martin, 2021; Munjal and Lecuit, 2014; Murrell et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Water flow and the resulting increase in hydrostatic pressure serve as another mechanical mechanism of cell shape change.
source: More recently, there is an accumulating body of work implicating a role of water flow and the resulting increase in hydrostatic pressure as another mechanical mechanism of cell shape change (Choudhury et al., 2022; Chugh et al., 2022; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In the osmotic engine model of cell migration, polarized distribution of ion channels and transporters generates an osmotic gradient that drives water inflow at the leading edge and outflow at the rear, leading to forward translocation of tumor cells in confined microenvironment.
source: For example, in the osmotic engine model of cell migration, polarized distribution of ion channels and transporters generates an osmotic gradient that drives water inflow at the leading edge and outflow at the rear, leading to forward translocation of tumor cells in confined microenvironment (Stroka et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Hydrostatic pressure from the extracellular environment can drive tissue morphogenesis, as demonstrated during mouse blastocyst formation, development of the otic vesicle in the zebrafish, and blood vessel lumen expansion.
source: Additionally, hydrostatic pressure from the extracellular environment can drive tissue morphogenesis, as demonstrated during mouse blastocyst formation (Chan et al., 2019; Dumortier et al., 2019), development of the otic vesicle in the zebrafish (Mosaliganti et al., 2019), and blood vessel lumen expansion (Gebala et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: EC migration persists after the inhibition of actin polymerization and in the absence of filopodia to generate new blood vessels in the zebrafish.
source: We have previously discovered that EC migration persists after the inhibition of actin polymerization and in the absence of filopodia to generate new blood vessels in the zebrafish (Phng et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Aquaporins are transmembrane water channels that increase water permeability of cell membranes to promote transcellular water flow.
source: In this study, we sought to determine whether hydrostatic pressure regulates EC migration during sprouting angiogenesis in the zebrafish by investigating the function of Aquaporins (Aqp), which are transmembrane water channels that increase water permeability of cell membranes to promote transcellular water flow (Day et al., 2014; Farinas et al., 1997; Kozono et al., 2002; Preston et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: ECs of newly formed intersegmental vessels (ISVs) express aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA.
source: We discovered that ECs of newly formed intersegmental vessels (ISVs) express aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA, and observed the enrichment of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 proteins in the leading edge of migrating tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 proteins are enriched in the leading edge of migrating tip cells.
source: We discovered that ECs of newly formed intersegmental vessels (ISVs) express aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA, and observed the enrichment of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 proteins in the leading edge of migrating tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Endothelial tip cells lacking aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 expression have reduced cell volume, membrane protrusions, and migration capacity.
source: Detailed single-cell analyses showed that endothelial tip cells lacking aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 expression have reduced cell volume, membrane protrusions, and migration capacity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: There is defective sprouting angiogenesis and ISV formation in aqp1a.1;aqp8a.1 double mutant zebrafish.
source: As a result, there is defective sprouting angiogenesis and ISV formation in aqp1a.1;aqp8a.1 double mutant zebrafish.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: When actin polymerization is inhibited in aqp1a.1;aqp8a.1 double mutant zebrafish, there is a greater impairment in EC migration and sprouting angiogenesis.
source: Notably, when actin polymerization is inhibited in aqp1a.1;aqp8a.1 double mutant zebrafish, there is a greater impairment in EC migration and sprouting angiogenesis, demonstrating the additive function of actin polymerization and hydrostatic pressure (that is created by water inflow) in generating membrane protrusions to drive EC migration in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Actin polymerization and hydrostatic pressure have additive functions in generating membrane protrusions to drive EC migration in vivo.
source: Notably, when actin polymerization is inhibited in aqp1a.1;aqp8a.1 double mutant zebrafish, there is a greater impairment in EC migration and sprouting angiogenesis, demonstrating the additive function of actin polymerization and hydrostatic pressure (that is created by water inflow) in generating membrane protrusions to drive EC migration in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Of the 18 aquaporin genes that are expressed in zebrafish, aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA have been detected in blood ECs.
source: Of the 18 aquaporin genes that are expressed in zebrafish (Tingaud-Sequeira et al., 2010), aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA have been detected in blood ECs (Koun et al., 2016; Rehn et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The endothelial expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 was confirmed at 30 hr post fertilization (hpf) and 2, 3, and 4 days post fertilization (dpf) by whole-mount in situ hybridization.
source: We confirmed the endothelial expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 at 30 hr post fertilization (hpf) and 2, 3, and 4 days post fertilization (dpf) by whole-mount in situ hybridization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: aqp1a.1 is widely expressed in blood vessels of the head and trunk (dorsal aorta [DA], caudal artery [CA], ISVs, dorsal longitudinal anastomotic vessels [DLAV] and caudal vein plexus) at 30 hpf.
source: While aqp1a.1 is widely expressed in blood vessels of the head and trunk (dorsal aorta [DA], caudal artery [CA], ISVs, dorsal longitudinal anastomotic vessels [DLAV] and caudal vein plexus) at 30 hpf, aqp8a.1 expression is absent in cerebral blood vessels and is restricted to the DA, CA, and the ventral regions of ISVs in the trunk.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: aqp8a.1 expression is absent in cerebral blood vessels and is restricted to the DA, CA, and the ventral regions of ISVs in the trunk at 30 hpf.
source: While aqp1a.1 is widely expressed in blood vessels of the head and trunk (dorsal aorta [DA], caudal artery [CA], ISVs, dorsal longitudinal anastomotic vessels [DLAV] and caudal vein plexus) at 30 hpf, aqp8a.1 expression is absent in cerebral blood vessels and is restricted to the DA, CA, and the ventral regions of ISVs in the trunk.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: After 1 dpf, aqp8a.1 expression expands to the entire ISV and DLAV.
source: After 1 dpf, aqp8a.1 expression expands to the entire ISV and DLAV.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 gradually decreases in the DA and CA so that both are absent by 4 dpf.
source: Additionally, the expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 gradually decreases in the DA and CA so that both are absent by 4 dpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) of ECs isolated at 24 hpf, 34 hpf, and 3 dpf confirmed the endothelial expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) of ECs isolated at 24 hpf, 34 hpf, and 3 dpf further confirmed the endothelial expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F), revealed differential expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA in distinct endothelial clusters, and highlighted elevated aqp1a.1 transcript expression in all endothelial subtypes compared to aqp8a.1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: scRNAseq revealed differential expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA in distinct endothelial clusters.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) of ECs isolated at 24 hpf, 34 hpf, and 3 dpf further confirmed the endothelial expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F), revealed differential expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA in distinct endothelial clusters, and highlighted elevated aqp1a.1 transcript expression in all endothelial subtypes compared to aqp8a.1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: scRNAseq highlighted elevated aqp1a.1 transcript expression in all endothelial subtypes compared to aqp8a.1.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) of ECs isolated at 24 hpf, 34 hpf, and 3 dpf further confirmed the endothelial expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F), revealed differential expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA in distinct endothelial clusters, and highlighted elevated aqp1a.1 transcript expression in all endothelial subtypes compared to aqp8a.1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: At 20 hpf, aqp1a.1 mRNA is highly expressed in the DA with little expression in the posterior cardinal vein (PCV).
source: At 20 hpf, aqp1a.1 mRNA is highly expressed in the DA with little expression in the posterior cardinal vein (PCV) (Figure 1A and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: At 20 hpf, aqp1a.1 expression is heterogeneous in the DA, with higher expression in ECs that would be specified as tip cells.
source: Closer inspection uncovered heterogeneous expression in the DA, with higher expression in ECs that would be specified as tip cells (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Tip cells of newly formed vascular sprouts express higher levels of aqp1a.1 compared to adjacent ECs in the DA at 20 hpf.
source: Indeed, tip cells of newly formed vascular sprouts express higher levels of aqp1a.1 compared to adjacent ECs in the DA at 20 hpf (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B) and the majority of ISVs (61%) display higher aqp1a.1 expression in tip cells than in trailing stalk cells at 22 hpf (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The majority of ISVs (61%) display higher aqp1a.1 expression in tip cells than in trailing stalk cells at 22 hpf.
source: Indeed, tip cells of newly formed vascular sprouts express higher levels of aqp1a.1 compared to adjacent ECs in the DA at 20 hpf (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B) and the majority of ISVs (61%) display higher aqp1a.1 expression in tip cells than in trailing stalk cells at 22 hpf (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1G.

claim: Aqp8a.1 expression is largely absent in the DA at 20 hpf.
source: Aqp8a.1 expression is at first largely absent in the DA at 20 hpf (Figure 1B and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C) but becomes detectable at 22 hpf (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Aqp8a.1 expression becomes detectable in the DA at 22 hpf.
source: Aqp8a.1 expression is at first largely absent in the DA at 20 hpf (Figure 1B and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C) but becomes detectable at 22 hpf (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1.

claim: aqp8a.1 expression is undetectable in tip cells of emerging ISVs at 20 hpf.
source: Interestingly, unlike aqp1a.1, aqp8a.1 expression is undetectable in tip cells of emerging ISVs at 20 hpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1.

claim: At 22 hpf, aqp8a.1 is expressed in 22 out of 23 tip cells analyzed, with 78% of ISVs exhibiting higher aqp8a.1 mRNA expression in stalk cells than tip cells.
source: At 22 hpf, it is expressed in 22 out of 23 tip cells analyzed, with 78% of ISVs exhibiting higher aqp8a.1 mRNA expression in stalk cells than tip cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1G.

claim: aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 are differentially expressed in newly formed vascular sprouts, with aqp1a.1 expression enriched in tip cells and aqp8a.1 expression in stalk cells.
source: These observations highlight differential expression pattern of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 in newly formed vascular sprouts, with aqp1a.1 expression enriched in tip cells and aqp8a.1 expression in stalk cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Treatment with 1 µM ki8751 from 20 hpf suppressed aqp1a.1 mRNA expression by 52% (p<0.0001) after 6 hr compared to DMSO-treated embryos.
source: Relative quantitative PCR (qPCR) experiments showed that aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA expression was suppressed by 52% (p<0.0001) and 17% (p=0.0028), respectively, after 6 hr of ki8751 treatment compared to DMSO-treated embryos (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1H.

claim: Treatment with 1 µM ki8751 from 20 hpf suppressed aqp8a.1 mRNA expression by 17% (p=0.0028) after 6 hr compared to DMSO-treated embryos.
source: Relative quantitative PCR (qPCR) experiments showed that aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA expression was suppressed by 52% (p<0.0001) and 17% (p=0.0028), respectively, after 6 hr of ki8751 treatment compared to DMSO-treated embryos (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1H.

claim: VEGFR2 activity upregulates the expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1.
source: These results demonstrate that VEGFR2 activity upregulates the expression of aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1H.

claim: Inhibition of VEGFR2 activity with 1 nM ki8751 decreased AQP1 mRNA expression by 31% (p=0.0023) in human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs).
source: Inhibition of VEGFR2 activity with 1 nM and 10 nM ki8751 decreased AQP1 mRNA expression by 31% (p=0.0023, Figure 1I) and 40% (Pp0.1032, Figure 1I), respectively, demonstrating cross-species conservation of VEGFR2 activity in inducing Aqp1 mRNA expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1I.

claim: Inhibition of VEGFR2 activity with 10 nM ki8751 decreased AQP1 mRNA expression by 40% (p=0.1032) in human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs).
source: Inhibition of VEGFR2 activity with 1 nM and 10 nM ki8751 decreased AQP1 mRNA expression by 31% (p=0.0023, Figure 1I) and 40% (Pp0.1032, Figure 1I), respectively, demonstrating cross-species conservation of VEGFR2 activity in inducing Aqp1 mRNA expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1I.

claim: There is cross-species conservation of VEGFR2 activity in inducing Aqp1 mRNA expression.
source: Inhibition of VEGFR2 activity with 1 nM and 10 nM ki8751 decreased AQP1 mRNA expression by 31% (p=0.0023, Figure 1I) and 40% (Pp0.1032, Figure 1I), respectively, demonstrating cross-species conservation of VEGFR2 activity in inducing Aqp1 mRNA expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1I.

claim: At 25 hpf, Aqp1a.1 accumulates in mCherryCAAX-positive membrane clusters in the cytoplasm and filopodia of tip cells.
source: At 25 hpf, we observed an accumulation of Aqp1a.1 (Figure 2A) and Aqp8a.1 (Figure 2B) in mCherryCAAX-positive membrane clusters in the cytoplasm and filopodia of tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: At 25 hpf, Aqp8a.1 accumulates in mCherryCAAX-positive membrane clusters in the cytoplasm and filopodia of tip cells.
source: At 25 hpf, we observed an accumulation of Aqp1a.1 (Figure 2A) and Aqp8a.1 (Figure 2B) in mCherryCAAX-positive membrane clusters in the cytoplasm and filopodia of tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: Many of the Aqp1a.1- or Aqp8a.1-positive membrane clusters are located at the migrating front of the tip cell.
source: Notably, many of the Aqp1a.1- or Aqp8a.1-positive membrane clusters are located at the migrating front of the tip cell.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Time-lapse imaging capturing the process of ISV formation between 24 hpf and 30 hpf showed sustained enrichment of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 in clusters at the front of the tip cell as well as in filopodia.
source: Time-lapse imaging capturing the process of ISV formation between 24 hpf and 30 hpf further showed sustained enrichment of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 in clusters at the front of the tip cell as well as in filopodia (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—videos 1 and 2), suggesting that Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 may promote localized water flux at the migrating edge of tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C and D.

claim: Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 may promote localized water flux at the migrating edge of tip cells.
source: Time-lapse imaging capturing the process of ISV formation between 24 hpf and 30 hpf further showed sustained enrichment of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 in clusters at the front of the tip cell as well as in filopodia (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—videos 1 and 2), suggesting that Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 may promote localized water flux at the migrating edge of tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a suggestion based on the localization data.

claim: The CRISPR-generating allele aqp1a.1rk28 carries a 14 bp deletion and an 8 bp insertion in the 5′ end of the gene, leading to a premature termination codon at amino acid 76 after 1 missense amino acid.
source: The CRISPR-generating allele aqp1a.1rk28 carries a 14 bp deletion and an 8 bp insertion in the 5′ end of the gene, leading to a premature termination codon at amino acid 76 after 1 missense amino acid (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The aqp8a.1rk29 allele carries a 4 bp deletion in the 5′ end of the gene that leads to a frameshift after Thr15 and premature termination codon at amino acid 73 after 58 missense amino acids.
source: The aqp8a.1rk29 allele carries a 4 bp deletion in the 5′ end of the gene that leads to a frameshift after Thr15 and premature termination codon at amino acid 73 after 58 missense amino acids (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA expression is significantly decreased in aqp1a.1rk28/rk28 and aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 zebrafish embryos, respectively.
source: Using whole-mount in situ hybridization and qPCR analysis, we demonstrated that aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA expression is significantly decreased in aqp1a.1rk28/rk28 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D) and aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D) zebrafish embryos, respectively, suggesting a rapid degradation of mutant mRNAs and as a result, the loss of Aquaporin protein expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: The decrease in aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA in mutant embryos suggests a rapid degradation of mutant mRNAs and as a result, the loss of Aquaporin protein expression.
source: Using whole-mount in situ hybridization and qPCR analysis, we demonstrated that aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 mRNA expression is significantly decreased in aqp1a.1rk28/rk28 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D) and aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D) zebrafish embryos, respectively, suggesting a rapid degradation of mutant mRNAs and as a result, the loss of Aquaporin protein expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the mRNA expression data.

claim: aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos look morphologically normal compared to wildtype or aqp1a.1+/rk28;aqp8a.1+/rk29 embryos.
source: Although aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos look morphologically normal compared to wildtype or aqp1a.1+/rk28;aqp8a.1+/rk29 embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A–D), we observed defects in blood vessel formation and patterning at 1–3 dpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Defects in blood vessel formation and patterning are observed in aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos at 1–3 dpf.
source: Although aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos look morphologically normal compared to wildtype or aqp1a.1+/rk28;aqp8a.1+/rk29 embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A–D), we observed defects in blood vessel formation and patterning at 1–3 dpf.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3.

claim: ISVs of aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos are much less developed at 28 hpf compared to control embryos.
source: Compared to 28 hpf control embryos whose ISVs have reached the dorsal roof of the neural tube and started to form the DLAV, ISVs of aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos are much less developed (Figure 3A and D) with significantly reduced length (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3H and K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3.

claim: ISVs of aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos have significantly reduced length at 28 hpf.
source: Compared to 28 hpf control embryos whose ISVs have reached the dorsal roof of the neural tube and started to form the DLAV, ISVs of aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos are much less developed (Figure 3A and D) with significantly reduced length (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3H and K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3E.

claim: The loss of aqp1a.1 leads to a greater decrease in ISV length than the loss of aqp8a.1.
source: Comparison of ISV length in aqp1a.1rk28/rk28, aqp8a.1rk29/rk29, and aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos shows that the loss of aqp1a.1 leads to a greater decrease in ISV length than the loss of aqp8a.1 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3I and J), and that the loss of both aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 results in the greatest reduction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3E.

claim: The loss of both aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 results in the greatest reduction in ISV length.
source: Comparison of ISV length in aqp1a.1rk28/rk28, aqp8a.1rk29/rk29, and aqp1a.1rk28/rk28;aqp8a.1rk29/rk29 embryos shows that the loss of aqp1a.1 leads to a greater decrease in ISV length than the loss of aqp8a.1 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3I and J), and that the loss of both aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 results in the greatest reduction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3E.

claim: There is an additive effect of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 function in blood vessel development.
source: These observations indicate an additive effect of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 function in blood vessel development and implicate Aqp1a.1 as the more dominant Aquaporin protein in EC function, in line with the higher expression of aqp1a.1 mRNA in tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the ISV length data.

claim: Aqp1a.1 is the more dominant Aquaporin protein in EC function, in line with the higher expression of aqp1a.1 mRNA in tip cells.
source: These observations indicate an additive effect of Aqp1a.1 and Aqp8a.1 function in blood vessel development and implicate Aqp1a.1 as the more dominant Aquaporin protein in EC function, in line with the higher expression of aqp1a.1 mRNA in tip cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the ISV length data and expression data.

claim: At 3 dpf, fully established ISVs are significantly reduced in embryos when aqp1a.1, aqp8a.1 or both aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 are deleted.
source: Such fully established ISVs are significantly reduced in embryos when aqp1a.1, aqp8a.1 or both aqp1a.1 and aqp8a.1 are deleted.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3.

claim: Aquaporin mutant embryos display an increased number of aISVs and vISVs that fail to establish a connection to the DLAV, DA, or PCV at 3 dpf.
source: Instead, these embryos display an increased number of aISVs and vISVs that fail to establish a connection to the DLAV, DA, or PCV (Figure 3H–J).
